tasks.title: Capture the claim description
tasks.description: Record what the policyholder reports: what happened, when, where, who was driving, and what was damaged. This description is what every later check in this process is run against — be as specific as the policyholder can be about the circumstances, not just the outcome (e.g. "reversed into a pole in a car park" rather than just "rear damage").

tasks.title: Confirm policy and incident validity
tasks.description: Check that the reported incident happened within the period of insurance shown on the certificate of insurance, and that it meets the policy's definition of a single incident (one event/accident/occurrence the policyholder didn't intend or expect — a series of related incidents from one cause still counts as one incident). If the incident falls outside the period of insurance, there is no cover to assess — go straight to a decision.

tasks.title: Check general exclusions
tasks.description: Screen the claim description against the policy's general exclusions before looking at any specific benefit. Key categories: driver impairment (alcohol/drugs, with an exception if the car was stolen or impairment wasn't a contributing factor); unlawful, unregistered, unlicensed, or reckless use; intentional/deliberate damage; racing or competition-track use; the car left unattended, unlocked, with keys in it; mechanical/electrical breakdown or wear and tear rather than an incident; use outside Australia; overloading; incorrect fuel; and use for hire, fare or reward (rideshare and car-pool are still covered). Several of these have narrow exceptions — check the linked clauses rather than relying on the category label alone. If a clear exclusion applies with no exception, this claim is not covered — go to the decision task. If none apply, continue.

tasks.title: Classify which specific cover applies
tasks.description: Based on what was damaged and how, determine which benefit the claim falls under: Accidental loss or damage to the policyholder's own car (the general benefit — hail, storm, flood, fire, theft, malicious damage, collision, impact); Third Party Property Damage (the policyholder's legal liability for damage to someone else's property, up to $20 million per incident); or Windscreen and window glass cover (only applies when the ONLY damage from the incident is to the windscreen/window glass/sunroof). tasks.title: Verify the claim is adequately evidenced
tasks.description: Confirm the policyholder can demonstrate the incident actually happened as described — request police reports, photographs, witness statements, or expert reports as appropriate. This step matters most where a general-exclusion exception turns on facts (e.g. "not aware further damage could occur", "could not have reasonably known" about an unlicensed driver, or the not-at-fault details below). If the incident can't be evidenced, the claim cannot be paid regardless of what cover would otherwise apply — route to manual review rather than a straight decision, since this is a judgment call on sufficiency, not a clean rule.

tasks.title: Determine settlement path: repair or total loss
tasks.description: Decide whether the car is repairable or a total loss. It's a total loss when it's uneconomical or unsafe to repair — including where combined repair cost plus salvage value would likely exceed the amount covered — with reference to the relevant State/Territory's legal write-off criteria. For a stolen car: if found within 14 days, treat as a repair claim; if not found within 14 days and the theft claim is accepted, it becomes a total loss. On a total loss, the payout is the amount covered on the certificate (which already reflects market value factors) less deductions — excess, unpaid premium/instalments, and any hire-car-related excess.

tasks.title: Reach the coverage decision
tasks.description: Combine the outputs of the prior tasks into a decision: Covered (state which benefit, the excess payable, and the settlement path), Not covered (state which exclusion or validity failure applies, with its citation), or Partially covered (e.g. one piece of damage covered, another excluded — state each separately). Every decision communicated to the policyholder should be traceable back to the specific clause(s) that drove it.

tasks.title: Escalate to manual review
tasks.description: Route here when the process can't reach a clean decision on its own: evidence is insufficient to confirm the incident, an exclusion's exception turns on a genuine judgment call (e.g. "reasonable", "not aware"), two clauses point in different directions, or the document is silent on something this specific claim needs. Record what's unresolved and why — see the issue log for known open points — so the reviewing handler isn't starting from a blank page.

tasks.description: Confirm the identity of the policyholder matches the certificate of insurance before proceeding with claim validation
